reuse.why: Introduces applyWeekendRule/isOffDay and routes the moving case through them, and the new handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, but the daily-skip variant is handled beside the helper rather than by it at every site.

duplication.why: The 'daily schedule: drop off-days instead of moving' logic, with its own over-fetch heuristic (7+holidays, count*7+..., 3+holidays padding), is rewritten in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and schedule-template keeps a redundant outer skipWeekend ternary around a helper that already takes the flag.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday predicates and movement live in shared/schedules.ts and the new request handler sits with the other schedule handlers in server/schedules/app.ts, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes stay within the schedule date logic, its handler, types, tests and a release note; the frequency/holidays additions to parseRecurDate are needed by the feature.

maintainability.why: The move-vs-skip decision is still settled at each call site, so a future change to the rule (as steps 3-4 already show) must touch several places that diverge in shape and padding.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, branch on isDailyWeekendSkip and filter with isOffDay themselves instead of applyWeekendRule deciding skip vs move.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily-skip filtering is expressed as dates.find(!isOffDay) in getNextDate, .filter(!isOffDay).slice in getUpcomingDates and an early return in a forEach in getDatesInRange, each with a differently shaped look-ahead formula.

abstraction_drift.where: holidays parameter added to applyWeekendRule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the daily-schedule skip is handled outside the helper in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (schedule-template also keeps its own skipWeekend ternary around the call).
